claim.date_text_original: Sauckel centralization decree of 21 March 1942 through the August 1944 peak of registered non-German labour in the Reich
claim.spatial_precision: state-directed system with heterogeneous sites, populations and occupied-territory linkages
claim.summary: From 1942 through 1944, Nazi Germany operated a centrally directed, racially differentiated forced-labour system drawing on deported foreign civilians, prisoners of war, concentration-camp prisoners and other persecuted groups. The 21 March 1942 decree centralized labour deployment under Fritz Sauckel, specialist scholarship documents the mass foreign-labour regime, and USHMM synthesis records more than 7.5 million non-German workers registered in the Reich in August 1944, the overwhelming majority forced labourers. The atlas records a strong positive state-forced-labour claim without converting workforce totals into territorial prevalence or equating every coerced status with chattel slavery.
claim.notes: Reconciles legacy research-prototype claim ab1f826b-aecf-4f2b-a88a-bccf1eea4f9a into current post-M1 semantics. Related broader workbook-migrated claim 85bb684d-0aad-5410-a466-d3aad7f49c6f remains separate lineage. No new P-level is assigned. Generic Reich/modern-country practice polygon is rejected; authoritative forced-labour sites are eligible as evidence loci and historically dated jurisdiction geometry requires separate review.

territorial_practice.notes: Positive bounded classification for a centrally organized wartime forced-labour system. Do not infer uniform territorial prevalence, a single labour status, or one practice polygon from aggregate worker counts.
